You are doing an ADVERSARIAL, evidence-based audit of the "cold email" outreach engine in the Nxeon platform repo at /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres, single-node production). Do not trust any prior summary of this system, including anything you might infer was "already fixed" — verify everything yourself from the actual current file contents, actual DB state, and actual test runs. This is a re-audit after a round of fixes; your job is to find anything still wrong, anything the fixes missed, and anything the fixes broke.

## System overview (for orientation only — verify, don't assume)

Cold outreach to purchased/scraped B2B leads, sent from an isolated domain (trynxeon.com) via a dedicated relay VM, kept structurally separate from the platform's own transactional mail (nxeon.cloud / Mailcow). Core files: `lib/coldemail/*.ts` (pure logic — compliance, sender/renderer, classify, feedback, leaddb, import), `worker/coldemail.ts` (the send scheduler/sweep), `worker/coldemail-inbox.ts` (IMAP reply + bounce poller), `worker/index.ts` (registers the sweeps on a loop), `lib/actions-coldemail*.ts` (server actions for the admin UI), `prisma/schema.prisma` (Brand/SendingDomain/Inbox/EmailList/Contact/ColdCampaign/SequenceStep/ColdSend/Suppression/ConsentRecord/DeliverabilityEvent models).

## What changed most recently (verify each of these actually works, don't just check the diff exists)

1. `worker/coldemail.ts`: a "GUARDRAIL #5" was added in `processDueSends`'s per-send loop to re-check `isMailableStatus(contact.emailStatus)` immediately before sending (not just at scheduling time), marking the ColdSend SUPPRESSED if the contact went dead in between. Read the actual current code around this and confirm: is `emailStatus` actually selected in the `due` query so this check has real data to work with? Does the check correctly run BEFORE the send attempt for every code path (rotation pool AND non-rotation fallback)? Could a contact still slip through?

2. `worker/coldemail-inbox.ts`: a bounce/NDR detector (`looksLikeBounce` + `parseDsnBounce`) was added because bounces (from mailer-daemon/postmaster) were previously silently dropped at the "known contact" gate before ever reaching classification. Verify: does the bounce check actually run BEFORE the `if (!contact) return` gate? Read `parseDsnBounce`'s regex carefully — construct a few realistic synthetic DSN bodies (real-world Postfix/Exchange/Gmail bounce format text, both "Final-Recipient: rfc822; user@example.com" hard-bounce 5.1.1 style and a soft 4.2.2 mailbox-full style) and mentally (or by writing a tiny throwaway ts-node script importing the function, don't edit the real files) trace whether they'd correctly extract the email and correctly classify hard vs soft. Does `recordFeedback` genuinely get called with the right `FeedbackKind`? Is there any way a REAL reply from a real contact could be misclassified as a bounce and dropped (false positive on `looksLikeBounce`)? Look hard at the subject-regex — could a legitimate reply subject like "Re: delivery has failed for our shipment" false-positive?

3. `lib/coldemail/import.ts`: `EMAIL_RE` was tightened from a loose `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$` to a stricter alphanumeric-anchored pattern. Actually test this regex (write a throwaway script, don't edit real files) against: valid real-world addresses that should NOT be rejected (plus-addressing like `jane+tag@example.com`, subdomains like `user@mail.example.co.uk`, hyphenated domains, single-letter TLDs-adjacent edge cases like `.io`/`.co`, numeric-only local parts) AND the known bad artifacts it's supposed to reject (`%20office@kindredpest.com`, `.legacyri@gmail.com`, `mailto:info@piccolinomv.com`). Report any false positives (valid emails now wrongly rejected) — that would be a regression, not a fix.

4. `worker/coldemail-inbox.ts`: `Inbox.imapHost` was changed from the hostname `mail.nxeon.cloud` (which publicly resolves to the platform host, not Mailcow — confirmed broken) to the raw IP `10.20.0.10`, with an explicit `tls: { servername: "mail.nxeon.cloud" }` override added to the ImapFlow config since the cert doesn't cover the IP. Check the current live DB value of `Inbox.imapHost` (`SELECT id,email,"imapHost","imapPort","imapTls" FROM "Inbox";` via `sudo -u postgres psql nxeon -c "..."`) actually reflects this. If you have DB access, also check `Inbox."lastPolledAt"` / `"lastImapUid"` to see if the poller has run recently and successfully (a recent timestamp with no matching error in the worker journal is good evidence; use `journalctl -u nxeon-worker.service --since "-30 min" -o cat | grep -i coldemail` to check for live errors — read-only, do not restart anything).

5. Local Business Variant A/B step 4 copy was changed to no longer be byte-identical between variants (each now echoes its own variant's opening angle). Verify via DB: `SELECT c.name, s."bodyMarkdown" FROM "SequenceStep" s JOIN "ColdCampaign" c ON c.id=s."campaignId" WHERE c.name ILIKE '%Variant%' AND s."stepOrder"=4;` — confirm the two rows are actually different now.

## Also independently re-verify these (don't assume they're still true)

- Campaign overlap: is any contact currently targeted by more than one ACTIVE (non-DRAFT... well all are currently DRAFT, but check anyway) campaign in a way that would double-send once launched? `SELECT elm."contactId", COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) FROM "EmailListMember" elm JOIN "ColdCampaign" c ON c."listId"=elm."listId" GROUP BY elm."contactId" HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) > 1;` (some incidental overlap was previously accepted as minor — just report the count, don't panic over a small number, but flag if it's large).
- `worker/coldemail.ts`'s send path: confirm it is STILL using the per-inbox isolated `NxeonSmtpTransport` built from `Inbox.smtp*` fields (not a shared/platform transport) — read the actual current code, don't trust that this was fixed before and never regressed.
- Tracking/unsubscribe link domain: confirm links still resolve to the isolated sending domain (trynxeon.com-derived), not `nxeon.cloud`, by reading how `base`/`linkBase` is computed and passed to `buildMessage()` in the current file.
- Consent/compliance: is there anything a contact could receive without a `ConsentRecord`? Is the CAN-SPAM footer (`complianceFooter`/`renderFooterHtml`) actually included in every rendered message unconditionally, or is there a code path that could skip it?
- Run the full existing test suite (`cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsx --test test/coldemail-*.test.ts`) and `npx tsc --noEmit` — report pass/fail counts and any tsc errors, don't just assume they pass.
- `cold_email_sending_enabled` Setting and all `ColdCampaign.status` values — confirm nothing is live-sending right now (should all still be DRAFT / sending disabled) unless something changed.

## Ground rules

- This is READ-ONLY investigation plus small throwaway verification scripts (e.g. a one-off `npx tsx -e "..."` to test a regex or a pure function in isolation) — do NOT edit any real file in /opt/nxeon, do NOT restart any service, do NOT send any real email, do NOT modify the database.
- Every finding must cite the exact evidence (file:line, actual command output, actual regex test result) — "should be fine" or "looks correct" without evidence is not acceptable. If you can't verify something, say so explicitly rather than assuming.
- Rank findings CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW / MINOR, and separately confirm which of the 5 "recent changes" above are genuinely working vs. still broken vs. broken in a new way.

Report back a structured findings list. Be skeptical — the point of this audit is to catch what a previous pass (including fixes made under time pressure) might have missed or introduced.

  id                    String    @id @default(cuid())

  warmupStartedAt       DateTime?
  // Optional per-brand override of the platform daily cap; null = use the global

  dailySendCap          Int?
  // Complaint-rate circuit breaker: when tripped the send worker refuses this

  sendingPaused         Boolean   @default(false)
  pausedReason          String    @default("")
  createdAt             DateTime  @default(now())

  lists          EmailList[]

  sendingDomains SendingDomain[]

  @@index([createdAt])

---SendingDomain---

  id                     String              @id @default(cuid())
  brandId                String
  domain                 String // apex, e.g. try-brand.com
  subdomain              String              @default("mail") // outreach subdomain strategy (mail. / outreach.)
  isPrimary              Boolean             @default(false)
  status                 SendingDomainStatus @default(PENDING)
  // Authentication (RFC + Yahoogle/Outlook 2026). Config-only flags until a live
  // DNS verifier lands; the readiness panel reflects them.
  spfVerified            Boolean             @default(false)
  dkimVerified           Boolean             @default(false)
  dmarcVerified          Boolean             @default(false)
  dmarcPolicy            DmarcPolicy         @default(NONE)
  // Custom tracking domain (t.mail-brand.com) — shared tracking domains are
  // blocklisted and tank placement, so a custom one is a readiness requirement.
  trackingDomain         String              @default("")
  trackingDomainVerified Boolean             @default(false)
  // RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe supported on this domain's mail.
  oneClickUnsub          Boolean             @default(true)
  reputationScore        Int                 @default(100)
  addedAt                DateTime            @default(now())
  warmupStartedAt        DateTime?
  lastCheckedAt          DateTime?
  pausedReason           String              @default("")

  brand          Brand                 @relation(fields: [brandId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  events         DeliverabilityEvent[]

  @@index([brandId])
  @@index([status])

  id              String          @id @default(cuid())
  sendingDomainId String
  email           String          @unique

  status          InboxStatus     @default(WARMING)

  dailyCap        Int             @default(40)
  // Today's warmup-ramped allowance (recomputed by the warmup sweep). Never exceeds dailyCap.
  currentRampCap  Int             @default(5)
  warmupDay       Int             @default(0)
  warmupStartedAt DateTime?
  // Warmup plan (folded onto the inbox — one plan per inbox).
  strategy        WarmupStrategy  @default(STANDARD)
  warmupMode      WarmupMode      @default(HYBRID)
  startCap        Int             @default(5)
  targetCap       Int             @default(40)
  rampDays        Int             @default(21)

  sendWindowStart Int? // minutes-from-midnight
  sendWindowEnd   Int?
  minGapSeconds   Int             @default(100) // 90–120s between sends reads human
  healthScore     Int             @default(100)
  reputationScore Int             @default(100)
  lastSendAt      DateTime?
  pausedReason    String          @default("")
  createdAt       DateTime        @default(now())

  // ---- Overhaul Phase 1: real per-mailbox SMTP + IMAP credentials ----
  //
  // These make rotation real (each inbox sends from its OWN mailbox, not a shared
  // relay) and unlock reply capture. Passwords are stored ENCRYPTED via
  // lib/crypto-box (never plaintext, never logged). All fields default to empty:
  // an inbox with no creds NEVER connects — IMAP polling + reply-send stay inert
  // for it. A blank host is the single guard the poller/sender check.
  smtpHost     String    @default("")
  smtpPort     Int       @default(587)
  smtpUser     String    @default("")
  smtpPassEnc  String    @default("") // encryptSecret(...) — never plaintext
  smtpTls      Boolean   @default(false) // true = implicit TLS (465); false = STARTTLS (587)
  imapHost     String    @default("")
  imapPort     Int       @default(993)
  imapUser     String    @default("")
  imapPassEnc  String    @default("") // encryptSecret(...) — never plaintext
  imapTls      Boolean   @default(true)
  // Poller bookmark: highest IMAP UID ingested + last successful poll time.
  lastImapUid  Int       @default(0)
  lastPolledAt DateTime?

  sendingDomain SendingDomain         @relation(fields: [sendingDomainId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  warmupStates  WarmupState[]
  events        DeliverabilityEvent[]
  sends         ColdSend[]
  conversations Conversation[]

  @@index([sendingDomainId])
  @@index([status])
  @@index([lastSendAt])
}

# Cold Email Engine Re-Audit — Findings

Scope covered: `worker/coldemail.ts`, `worker/coldemail-inbox.ts`, `worker/coldemail-deliverability.ts`, `lib/coldemail/{compliance,sender,leaddb,feedback,import,classify,rotation}.ts`, `lib/actions-coldemail.ts`, `components/admin/coldemail/Controls.tsx`, live Postgres state, `journalctl -u nxeon-worker.service`, full test suite, `tsc --noEmit`, plus throwaway scripts (`/tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/test-email-re.mjs`, `test-tls.mjs`, `test-bounce.mjs`) exercising the actual regex/TLS/parsing logic copied verbatim from the real files. No real files were edited, no service restarted, no email sent, no DB rows changed.

## Status of the 5 claimed fixes

1. **GUARDRAIL #5 (mailability re-check at send time) — WORKING.** `worker/coldemail.ts:312` selects `emailStatus` in the `due` query; the check at `worker/coldemail.ts:334-337` runs before the rotation/non-rotation branch splits at line 339, so it's enforced on both code paths. Residual LOW risk: the `due` rows (and their `emailStatus`) are a snapshot taken once per sweep (≤50 rows, up to ~2 min with jitter), so a status change that lands mid-sweep isn't caught until the *next* sweep — acceptable given the documented threat model (multi-day gap between scheduling and firing), just not airtight to the second.

2. **Bounce/DSN detection — PARTIALLY WORKING, confirmed regression found.** `looksLikeBounce`/`parseDsnBounce` run before the `if (!contact) return` gate (`worker/coldemail-inbox.ts:184` vs `:197`) — correct. Tested against realistic synthetic Postfix (5.1.1), Exchange (4.2.2 mailbox-full), and Gmail-style DSNs via `mailparser`: all three extract the right email and correctly classify hard vs. soft, and `recordFeedback` is called with the right `FeedbackKind` per `resolveKind()`. **But** the subject-only fallback regex (`/undeliverable|delivery status notification|delivery has failed|returned to sender|failure notice|mail delivery (?:failed|subsystem)/i`) genuinely false-positives, confirmed by test: a synthetic real reply with subject `"Re: delivery has failed for our shipment"` (body: *"...yes I'm interested... can we set up a call this week?"*) and one with subject `"RE: Failure notice on our end, ignore previous email"` both trip `looksLikeBounce → true`; `parseDsnBounce` correctly returns `null` (no DSN structure) but the caller unconditionally `return`s after a WARN log. Net effect: a real, interested reply is **silently discarded** — no Conversation/Message row, contact not advanced to REPLIED, and critically the "halt remaining queued sends on reply" step (`:276-281`) never runs, so the person keeps receiving drip emails after having already replied. Also: `looksLikeBounce`/`parseDsnBounce` aren't exported and `test/coldemail-inbox.test.ts` never exercises them — this feature shipped with zero unit coverage.

3. **EMAIL_RE tightening — WORKING**, with one narrow regression. All three named bad artifacts (`%20office@...`, `.legacyri@gmail.com`, `mailto:info@...`) plus `user@`, `user@.com`, doubled dots, leading/trailing-hyphen labels all correctly rejected. All realistic valid forms pass (plus-addressing, subdomains, hyphenated/short-TLD domains, numeric local parts). One true regression: `o'brien@example.com` (apostrophe in local part, RFC-legal, occurs in real names) is now rejected — LOW severity, narrow.

4. **IMAP host/TLS fix — CONFIRMED WORKING NOW, but caused a real ~8-minute prod outage during rollout.** DB confirms `Inbox.imapHost = 10.20.0.10`, `imapTls = true`. I replicated ImapFlow's exact option-merge (`Object.assign({...,servername:false}, {servername:"mail.nxeon.cloud"})`) in a live TLS test against the real inbox IP: it connects and the cert's SAN is `mail.nxeon.cloud` — confirming the code as written is correct, and `lastPolledAt = 2026-08-26 04:20:08 UTC` / `lastImapUid = 3` in the DB shows a real successful poll. However, `journalctl` shows a live error window from **04:05:48 to 04:11:54 UTC today**: `"Hostname/IP does not match certificate's altnames: IP: 10.20.0.10 is not in the cert's list"` — the exact signature I reproduced when the servername override is *not* applied. The worker service (`systemctl status`) shows it restarted at 04:13:51, ~2 min after the last error. Read together: the DB's `imapHost` was flipped to the new IP before the long-lived `tsx` worker process had been restarted to pick up the code that adds the `tls.servername` override, so for ~8 minutes IMAP polling was actively broken in production with a *new* failure mode. Resolved now, but it's a deploy/runbook gap worth fixing (DB config change + coupled code change must land atomically, or trigger a restart).

5. **Variant A/B step 4 copy — CONFIRMED WORKING.** DB query shows genuinely different `bodyMarkdown` text between Variant A and Variant B at `stepOrder=4`.

## Additional findings (ranked)

**CRITICAL — isolated-relay fix is incomplete; the dangerous fallback is live-reachable right now.** `processDueSends` (`worker/coldemail.ts:340-383`) only builds a per-inbox `NxeonSmtpTransport` when `loadBrandRotationPool()` returns a non-empty pool. That function filters `where: { status: "ACTIVE", ... }` (`:70`) — but the DB's only configured inbox is currently `status = 'WARMING'`, so the pool is `[]` today. When the pool is empty, `chosen` stays `null` for every row and `transport` falls back to `ctx.transport`, built once via `getTransport("nxeon-smtp")` → `loadSmtpConfig()` (`lib/coldemail/sender.ts:325-341`), which reads the **exact same** `smtp_host/port/user/pass/secure` Settings that `lib/mailer.ts:48` uses for the platform's own transactional email. This is precisely the bug commit `35e69ba` claims to have fixed — the fix only covers the rotation-pool branch, not this pre-existing Phase-2 fallback, which is fully intact. Since new inboxes default to a 21-day warmup ramp before auto-promotion to `ACTIVE` (`worker/coldemail-deliverability.ts:85`, `rampDays` default 21), this isn't a one-day fluke — it's the default state for the first three weeks of any inbox's life, which is exactly when a first campaign is likely to be test-launched. Note: the From-address/tracking-link domain does **not** leak in this fallback (still derived from `brand.fromEmail = hello@trynxeon.com`), so the isolation break is specifically at the transport/relay level — cold outreach would physically route through the platform's Mailcow relay while claiming a trynxeon.com identity, almost certainly failing SPF alignment and contaminating the platform's transactional-mail reputation, which is the exact risk this architecture is meant to prevent.

**HIGH — bounce-detection false positive silently drops real replies and keeps emailing people who already responded.** See fix #2 above — reproduced with concrete synthetic evidence, not speculation.

**HIGH — ConsentRecord is not enforced anywhere in the send path.** `db.consentRecord` rows are only written when an import explicitly opts in (`recordConsent` form checkbox, defaulting to unchecked; `IngestOptions.recordConsent` defaults to `false` in `lib/coldemail/import.ts:305`). The only place `consentRecords` is consulted is a preview/reporting function (`lib/actions-coldemail.ts:~630-683`) that counts a `missingConsent` bucket purely for display — it does not block scheduling. Neither `scheduleCampaignSends` nor `processDueSends` in `worker/coldemail.ts` ever checks for a ConsentRecord; the only gates are `isMailableStatus` and `isSuppressed`. Today's DB happens to show 7146 contacts / 7146 consent rows (1:1), so it isn't actively exploited, but nothing structurally prevents a future import (or any other contact-creation path) from producing sendable contacts with zero consent evidence.

**MEDIUM — self-attested compliance checkbox coexists with the "live DNS, never a manual checkbox" claim.** `saveBrand` (`lib/actions-coldemail.ts:466-504`) still writes `Brand.spfVerified/dkimVerified/dmarcVerified` directly from admin-form checkboxes rendered in `BrandForm` (`components/admin/coldemail/Controls.tsx:496-502`), and these are the exact fields `evaluateSendEligibility`/`requireBrandCompliance` gate the worker's per-campaign send eligibility on (GUARDRAILS #2/#3). `verifyBrandDns` (the real DNS-lookup path) writes to the same fields with a comment saying this should "never" be a manual checkbox — but the manual path is still live and reachable in parallel. Currently the stored values happen to match real DNS state, so it's not currently exploited, but any platform-admin session can flip a brand green without any actual verification.

**MEDIUM — IMAP fix rollout caused a real, if now-resolved, production incident** (see fix #4).

**MEDIUM — zero unit-test coverage for the bounce-detection feature** (see fix #2); the only verification that ever existed for this code was the throwaway script written for this audit.

**LOW — `o'brien@example.com`-style apostrophe local-parts rejected** by the tightened `EMAIL_RE` (fix #3).

**LOW — guardrail suppression/mailability lists are sweep-scoped snapshots**, so an in-flight status change within the same ≤50-send/≤2-minute sweep isn't caught until the next sweep (affects both GUARDRAIL #4 and #5 identically; not a new issue, just worth naming precisely).

## Independently re-verified as OK

- **Campaign overlap:** only 2 contacts are members of 2 campaign lists each — negligible, per the audit's own threshold.
- **Tracking/unsubscribe link domain:** correctly isolated to `trynxeon.com` in both the rotation and fallback paths (`worker/coldemail.ts:360-361` derives `linkBase` from `sendIdentity.fromEmail`, always a trynxeon.com address today).
- **Compliance footer:** unconditionally included — `buildMessage()` (`lib/coldemail/sender.ts:248-263`) always computes and appends it; no skip path exists.
- **Test suite:** `npx tsx --test test/coldemail-*.test.ts` → 119/119 pass, 0 failures.
- **`tsc --noEmit`:** clean, 0 errors.
- **Nothing is live-sending:** no `cold_email_sending_enabled` Setting row exists in the DB (defaults to `false`); all 6 `ColdCampaign` rows are `DRAFT`; `ColdSend` table is empty (0 rows).
